title: The Sunken Pirate Token
complaint: Hi! I'm Leo. I'm in the final room of the Pirate Cove Escape Adventure, but the last gold pirate token is stuck at the bottom of a tall, narrow glass tube bolted to the floor!
obvious_trap: Tying a magnet to a string and lowering it down the tube to pull the coin up.
hidden_constraint: The shiny pirate coin is made of lightweight plastic, not metal, so the magnet will not stick to it.
on_hand_items: A plastic pitcher full of drinking water
A pair of metal safety scissors
A handful of dry macaroni noodles

clue_cards.title: Float It Up
clue_cards.insight: Lightweight plastic objects like the coin will float if they are surrounded by liquid.

clue_cards.title: Sticky Situation
clue_cards.insight: If a magnet won't grab the prize, something sticky on the end of a long object might do the trick.

clue_cards.title: Reach the Bottom
clue_cards.insight: You need a rigid or semi-rigid item that is long enough to touch the bottom of the tube to fetch the coin.

potential_solutions.title: Float the Treasure
potential_solutions.description: Pour the water from the plastic pitcher straight into the glass tube. Because the coin is made of plastic, it will float all the way up to the top where you can grab it.

potential_solutions.title: The Sticky Stick
potential_solutions.description: Chew the bubblegum until it is nice and sticky, press it firmly onto the end of the wooden drumstick, and lower it down the tube to stick to the coin and lift it out.

potential_solutions.title: Tape and Rope Plumb Line
potential_solutions.description: Wrap a piece of the double-sided tape around the very end of the plastic jump rope. Lower the taped end down the tube until it hits the coin, press down hard, and pull your prize up.

title: The Sunken Pirate Key
complaint: Hi! I'm Maya. I am in a pirate-themed escape room and almost finished! But the final shiny key slipped from my hand and fell to the bottom of a tall, narrow plastic pipe bolted to the wall.
obvious_trap: Tying the fridge magnet to the yarn and lowering it down the pipe to attract and catch the shiny key.
hidden_constraint: The shiny key is actually made of metallic-painted plastic, so the magnet will not stick to it at all.

clue_cards.title: Material Check
clue_cards.insight: Magnets only pull on certain metals. Just because the key looks shiny like gold or silver doesn't mean it is actually metal!

clue_cards.title: Sticky Situation
clue_cards.insight: If a magnet won't grab the key, maybe something sticky from your pocket can grab a lightweight object just as well.

clue_cards.title: Going Fishing
clue_cards.insight: You have items that can be bent and shaped. Think about how you might make a hook to catch the hole in the key.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 1: Sticky Gum Drop
potential_solutions.description: Chew the bubblegum until it is nice and sticky, wrap the end of the yarn tightly around it, and lower it down the pipe to stick to the plastic key and pull it up.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 2: Pipe Cleaner Hook
potential_solutions.description: Bend the fuzzy pipe cleaner into a hook shape, tie it securely to the end of the yarn, and lower it down the pipe to hook through the hole at the top of the key.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 3: The Long Tape Grabber
potential_solutions.description: Tape the unsharpened pencil to the wooden ruler to make a long stick, then wrap masking tape sticky-side out around the bottom end. Reach down the pipe and press it onto the key to lift it out.

title: The Glass Tube Trap
complaint: Hi! I'm Chloe. I am playing a wizard-themed escape room at my friend's birthday party and the timer is running out! I can see the final key at the bottom of a tall, narrow glass tube bolted to the floor, but my arm is too short and wide to reach inside.
obvious_trap: Tying the small fridge magnet to the long shoelace to fish the key out of the tube.
hidden_constraint: The final key is made of solid brass, which is completely non-magnetic, so the fridge magnet will not stick to it at all.
on_hand_items: A piece of sticky wall putty

clue_cards.title: Material Check
clue_cards.insight: Will a magnet actually stick to a shiny yellow metal like brass? You might need to find a different way to grab it.

clue_cards.title: Sticky Situation
clue_cards.insight: If magnetism fails, what do you have that is sticky enough to hold the key, and long enough to reach the bottom of the tube?

clue_cards.title: Catch and Release
clue_cards.insight: Keys usually have a hole at the top. Look at your items to see if anything can be bent to catch that hole.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 1: The Sticky Stick
potential_solutions.description: Wrap some scotch tape around the wooden dowel to attach the sticky wall putty to the very tip. Reach down the tube, press the putty firmly against the brass key, and lift it straight up.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 2: The Fishing Hook
potential_solutions.description: Unbend the metal paperclip and shape it into a hook. Tie the long shoelace tightly to the other end of the paperclip, then lower it down the tube to hook through the hole in the top of the key.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 3: The Straw Lasso
potential_solutions.description: Thread the long shoelace completely through the plastic drinking straw so a loop sticks out the bottom. Use the stiff straw to guide the loop over the key, pull the top strings tight to grip it, and lift the key out.

title: The Sunken Pirate Key
complaint: Hi! I'm Toby. I'm in the final room of a pirate escape game, but the last key is stuck at the bottom of a tall, narrow plastic pipe bolted to the floor!
obvious_trap: Tying the fridge magnet to the shoelace to lower it down and grab the key like a fishing pole.
hidden_constraint: The pirate key is actually made of lightweight plastic, not metal, so the magnet will not stick to it at all.

clue_cards.title: Check the Material
clue_cards.insight: Look closely at the key through the clear pipe. Does it look shiny and heavy like real metal, or is it brightly colored?

clue_cards.title: Sticky Situation
clue_cards.insight: If a magnet won't work, do you have anything else that can grab onto objects by touching them?

clue_cards.title: Up, Up, and Away
clue_cards.insight: The pipe is completely sealed at the bottom. What happens to lightweight plastic toys when you drop them in a swimming pool?

potential_solutions.title: Solution 1: The Floating Key
potential_solutions.description: Pour the full bottle of water directly into the plastic pipe. Since the key is made of lightweight plastic, it will float right up to the top where Toby can grab it.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 2: Sticky Fishing Line
potential_solutions.description: Wrap the sticky bubblegum around the heavy glass marble, tie the marble to the shoelace, and lower it down so the gum sticks to the plastic key.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 3: The Tape Trap
potential_solutions.description: Roll a piece of masking tape inside out so it is sticky on all sides, attach it to the bottom of the shoelace using the metal paperclip as a weight, and drop it down to fetch the key.

title: The Sunken Treasure Key
complaint: Hi! I'm Oliver. I'm in a pirate-themed escape room for my friend's birthday party, and the final treasure key is stuck at the bottom of a really long, narrow plastic pipe bolted to the floor!
obvious_trap: Tying the shoelace to the fridge magnet and lowering it down the pipe to magically snap onto the key and pull it up.
hidden_constraint: The key is actually made of lightweight plastic painted to look like gold, so it is completely non-magnetic.

clue_cards.title: Material Check
clue_cards.insight: Magnets only stick to certain metals. What if that shiny gold key is actually a trick?

clue_cards.title: Floating Idea
clue_cards.insight: If the key is actually made of hollow, lightweight plastic, think about how plastic reacts when dropped in a pool.

clue_cards.title: Sticky Grabber
clue_cards.insight: If a magnet won't stick, you might need something gooey or sticky to grab the key instead.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 1: The Water Ride
potential_solutions.description: Pour the pitcher of tap water directly into the plastic pipe. Because the key is made of lightweight plastic, it will float all the way to the top of the pipe so you can just grab it with your hands.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 2: The Sticky Drop
potential_solutions.description: Tie the shoelace around the heavy iron bolt so it has enough weight to drop straight down the pipe. Stick the chewed bubblegum to the bottom of the bolt, lower it until it touches the key, press down slightly, and carefully pull the key up.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 3: The Fishing Hook
potential_solutions.description: Unbend the metal paperclip and bend one end into a hook shape. Use the clear tape to safely attach the hooked paperclip to the end of the shoelace, lower it down the pipe, and hook it through the hole in the key to fish it out.

setting: A dimly lit, Victorian-themed escape room
title: The Pipe Dream
complaint: Hi! I'm Zoe. My friends and I are in the final stage of a Victorian-themed escape room with only five minutes left on the clock, but the final exit key just slipped from my hand and fell straight down a three-foot vertical pipe bolted to the wall!
obvious_trap: Tying a magnet to a shoelace and lowering it down the pipe to magnetically catch the key.
hidden_constraint: The final exit key is made of solid brass, meaning it is completely non-magnetic and will not stick to the magnet no matter how close it gets.

clue_cards.title: Check Your Metals
clue_cards.insight: Not all shiny metals are magnetic. Look closely with your flashlight at the color of the key at the bottom of the pipe to see if it's iron or brass.

clue_cards.title: A Sticky Situation
clue_cards.insight: If an invisible magnetic pull won't work, you'll need something that can physically grab the surface of the key on contact.

clue_cards.title: Fishing for Answers
clue_cards.insight: Every key has a small hole at the top for a keyring. A stiff, bendable item could act like a fishing hook.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 1: The Sticky Plunge
potential_solutions.description: Wrap several layers of double-sided tape tightly around the end of the wooden dowel. Shine the flashlight down the pipe to guide your aim, lower the dowel, and press it firmly against the flat side of the key so it sticks, then carefully pull it up.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 2: The Wire Hook
potential_solutions.description: Use your hands to completely unbend the wire coat hanger until it is a long, straight rod. Bend the very tip into a small J-shape hook, slide it down the pipe, and fish it through the keyhole ring to pull the key out.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 3: The Weighted Gum Drop
potential_solutions.description: Chew a piece of gum until it is extremely sticky. Mold the gum around the bottom of the horseshoe magnet (using the magnet purely as a heavy weight to keep the string straight, not for its magnetic properties). Tie the shoelace to the top of the magnet, drop it down the pipe, and press the gum firmly onto the key to lift it.

title: The Unreachable Key
complaint: Hi! I'm Elena. I am stuck in the final room of the 'Vintage Study' escape game, and there is a small key sitting at the very bottom of a tall, narrow glass vase bolted to the floor. I need that key to unlock the exit door, but the vase is too deep for my arm and I cannot tip it over!
obvious_trap: Tying a fridge magnet to a piece of yarn to fish the metal key out from the bottom of the vase.
hidden_constraint: The key is made of solid brass which is completely non-magnetic, and the vase opening is only two inches wide.
on_hand_items: a half-full bottle of drinking water
a roll of clear scotch tape

clue_cards.title: Material Matters
clue_cards.insight: Examine the color and material of the key. Not all metals will react to a magnet.

clue_cards.title: Sticky Situation
clue_cards.insight: If you cannot hook or magnetize the object, you might need to use something that grips on contact.

clue_cards.title: Reach Extension
clue_cards.insight: You need something long, stiff, and narrow enough to fit down a two-inch opening.

potential_solutions.title: The Sticky Plunge
potential_solutions.description: Chew the stick of gum until it becomes sticky, press it firmly onto the end of the wooden drumstick, and lower it down to pick up the key.

potential_solutions.title: The Hanger Hook
potential_solutions.description: Untwist the wire coat hanger to make a single long piece of metal wire, bend the tip into a small hook, and fish the key out by its hole.

potential_solutions.title: The Tape Snare
potential_solutions.description: Roll a piece of scotch tape inside out to form a sticky loop, attach it to the end of the unbent wire coat hanger, and press it against the key to pull it up.

title: The Brass Tax of Escaping
complaint: Hi! I'm Marcus. I'm locked in the final stage of the Billionaire's Vault escape room with only five minutes left on the clock! The final exit key is resting at the bottom of a narrow, four-foot-deep vertical glass tube bolted to the floor, but the opening is too small for my arm.
obvious_trap: Tying the cotton twine to the horseshoe magnet and lowering it down the tube to magnetically snap onto the key.
hidden_constraint: The exit key is made of solid brass, which is completely non-magnetic. The magnet will just sit uselessly on top of it without picking it up.

clue_cards.title: Material Matters
clue_cards.insight: Magnets only attract certain metals like iron or steel. Take a closer look at the color and material of that key.

clue_cards.title: Sticky Situation
clue_cards.insight: If an invisible magnetic force won't grab the key, you will need to find a way to physically stick to it instead.

clue_cards.title: Dropping Weight
clue_cards.insight: You need something heavy enough to drop down a straight line and press down firmly on the key. Look for heavy items you can tie a string to.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 1: The Sticky Flashlight
potential_solutions.description: Chew a piece of gum until it is sticky, press it firmly onto the flat bottom of the heavy flashlight, tie the cotton twine to the flashlight, and lower it down the tube to press the gum onto the key and pull it up.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 2: The Wire Hook
potential_solutions.description: Untwist and straighten out the wire coat hanger completely, bend a tiny, sharp hook at the very end, and carefully fish the key out by snagging the hole at the top of the key.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 3: The Heavy Tape Drop
potential_solutions.description: Wrap the double-sided tape entirely around the horseshoe magnet. Tie the magnet to the shoelaces and lower it down the tube, using the magnet purely as a heavy weight to forcefully press the sticky tape onto the brass key.

setting: Final stage of an Egyptian-themed Escape Room
title: The Pharaoh's Pipe
complaint: Hi! I'm David. I'm in the final stage of the 'Pharaoh's Tomb' escape room and we are minutes away from beating the all-time record. But my teammate just accidentally dropped the heavy final exit key down a narrow, 3-foot vertical glass tube set into the floor!
obvious_trap: Tying the fridge magnet to the string and lowering it down the glass tube to magnetically attract and pull up the key.
hidden_constraint: The final exit key is made of solid brass, which is completely non-magnetic, meaning the magnet will not stick to it at all.

clue_cards.title: Material Matters
clue_cards.insight: Magnets only attract ferrous metals like iron or steel. If a heavy object is made of brass, copper, or gold, a magnetic approach will completely fail.

clue_cards.title: Sticky Solutions
clue_cards.insight: When you cannot physically hook or magnetize a dropped object, applying a strong adhesive force directly to its flat surface is your best bet.

clue_cards.title: Rigid Control
clue_cards.insight: A string is great for lowering things, but it cannot apply downward pressure. You need a rigid object to press an adhesive firmly against your target.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 1: The Sticky Weight Drop
potential_solutions.description: Chew several pieces of gum until they are extremely sticky. Mold the gum onto the bottom of the fridge magnet (using the magnet merely as a heavy weight, not for magnetism). Tie the string to the magnet, lower it down the tube, and let the heavy weight of the magnet press the sticky gum firmly onto the brass key to lift it out.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 2: The Tape Spear
potential_solutions.description: Unbend the metal coat hanger to create a long, stiff rod. Wrap a piece of duct tape around the very tip inside-out so the sticky side is fully exposed. Shine the pocket flashlight down the tube to see, press the sticky hanger tip hard against the brass key to grab it, and pull it up.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 3: The Precision Hook
potential_solutions.description: Straighten out the metal coat hanger, but bend the very tip into a tiny, tight hook. Slide this long wire down the narrow glass tube, maneuver the hook through the keyring hole on the top of the brass key, and carefully hoist it to the surface.

setting: A dimly lit, dungeon-themed escape room with a ticking clock
title: The Glass Tube Dilemma
complaint: Hi! I'm Hannah. I'm locked in the final stage of a dungeon-themed escape room with only five minutes left on the clock, and the exit key is sitting right in front of me at the bottom of a three-foot-tall, vertical glass tube bolted firmly to the floor, but I can't reach it!
obvious_trap: Tie the fridge magnet to the shoelace and lower it down the tube to pull the metal key up magnetically.
hidden_constraint: The exit key is made of solid brass, which is entirely non-magnetic, and the opening of the glass tube is only one inch wide.
on_hand_items: A thin metal wire coat hanger

clue_cards.title: Material Check
clue_cards.insight: Not all shiny metals react to magnets. You might need to rely on friction, adhesives, or physical hooking to grab the prize.

clue_cards.title: Reach and Extend
clue_cards.insight: The tube is very narrow and deep. Look for items that can be unraveled or straightened to reach all the way to the bottom.

clue_cards.title: Tacky Tactics
clue_cards.insight: If you can't get a grip on the key with your hands, create a surface that the key will naturally stick to when pressed.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 1: The Sticky Wire
potential_solutions.description: Straighten out the metal wire coat hanger into a long pole. Chew a piece of gum until it is sticky, attach it securely to the tip of the wire, and press it firmly against the brass key to lift it out.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 2: Tape and String Drop
potential_solutions.description: Fold a piece of duct tape into a loop so the sticky side is facing outward, tie it securely to the end of the long cotton shoelace, and carefully lower it down the tube to stick to the key and hoist it up.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 3: Custom Wire Hook
potential_solutions.description: Untwist and straighten the metal wire coat hanger, then use the leverage of the metal scissors to bend the very end of the wire into a tiny, tight hook that can slip through the hole in the key to fish it out.

setting: The hallway right by the front door
title: The Floor Vent Fiasco
complaint: Hi! I'm Devon. I have to leave for the school bus in exactly three minutes or I'll miss the big field trip, but I just dropped my house key down the metal floor vent!
obvious_trap: Tying the fridge magnet to the shoelace and lowering it down the vent to magnetically pull the metal key back up.
hidden_constraint: The house key is made of solid brass (which is not magnetic), and the floor vent grate is made of steel, meaning the magnet will just instantly stick to the grate and won't even go down the hole.

clue_cards.title: Magnetic Mismatch
clue_cards.insight: Not all metals act the same! Test your magnet on different things first to see if it actually grabs them, and watch out for other metal objects in the way.

clue_cards.title: The Power of Stick
clue_cards.insight: If you can't pull something up with an invisible magnetic force, maybe you can use something gooey or sticky from your items to grab it.

clue_cards.title: Look for the Loop
clue_cards.insight: Think about the shape of the lost item. House keys always have a handy little hole at the top that is perfect for snagging if you can make a tiny hook.

potential_solutions.title: The Sticky Ruler
potential_solutions.description: Wrap a piece of masking tape around the end of the wooden ruler with the sticky side facing out. Slide the ruler down the vent slot and press it firmly against the brass key to lift it out.

potential_solutions.title: The Chewing Gum Harpoon
potential_solutions.description: Chew a piece of gum until it's nice and sticky, then mold it onto the end of the plastic drinking straw. Use the flashlight to see down the vent, poke the key with the gum, and carefully pull it up.

potential_solutions.title: The Paperclip Hook
potential_solutions.description: Unbend the metal paperclip to make a small hook. Tape the straight end of the paperclip to the wooden ruler (or tie it to the shoelace), lower it down the vent, snag the keyhole, and pull the key to safety.

setting: The hallway floor grate, 3 minutes before the school bus arrives
title: The Great Grate Rescue
complaint: Hi! I'm Carlos. I am rushing to catch the school bus in three minutes, but I just dropped my metal house key right down the narrow floor grate!
obvious_trap: Tie a fridge magnet to a shoelace and lower it down into the grate to catch the metal key.
hidden_constraint: The floor grate itself is made of solid steel, so the magnet will instantly snap to the sides of the grate and get stuck before it ever reaches the key at the bottom.
on_hand_items: A pair of sneakers with long shoelaces

clue_cards.title: Magnetic Attraction
clue_cards.insight: Magnets love keys, but they also love big heavy metal objects nearby. Ask what the floor grate is made out of!

clue_cards.title: Sticky Situation
clue_cards.insight: If a magnet gets stuck in the wrong place, you might need something sticky instead of magnetic.

clue_cards.title: Stiff and Steady
clue_cards.insight: A string or shoelace is floppy and hard to aim in a hurry. You need something long and stiff to reach down the narrow holes.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 1: The Coat Hanger Hook
potential_solutions.description: Unbend the wire coat hanger completely to make a long, stiff hook. Carefully lower it down the grate, hook it right through the key's metal ring, and pull it straight up.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 2: The Sticky Stick
potential_solutions.description: Wrap masking tape sticky-side out around the end of the wooden ruler. Shine the flashlight down to aim, and press the sticky tape directly against the key to pull it up.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 3: The Gum Grabber
potential_solutions.description: Chew a piece of gum to make it sticky, attach it firmly to the bottom tip of the wooden ruler or plastic straw, and press it firmly onto the flat part of the key to lift it out.

title: The Trapped Permission Slip
complaint: Hi! I'm Sophia. I'm standing by the front door because my school bus for the zoo field trip arrives in exactly five minutes! But my signed permission slip just fluttered behind my dad's giant, heavy bookshelf and I can't move the shelf to get it out.
obvious_trap: Use the thick wooden yardstick to reach down behind the shelf and push or slide the paper out.
hidden_constraint: The gap between the bookshelf and the wall is barely half an inch wide, making the thick wooden yardstick too fat to fit inside the crack.

clue_cards.title: Narrow Squeeze
clue_cards.insight: The gap is super thin. Look for long objects that are flat or wire-thin to easily reach down without getting stuck.

clue_cards.title: Sticky Situation
clue_cards.insight: Paper is very light and hard to grab. If you can't pinch it, maybe you can make it stick to something you lower down.

clue_cards.title: Weighted Line
clue_cards.insight: Yarn is long enough to reach the bottom but too floppy to drop straight. You might need something small and heavy to guide it down.

potential_solutions.title: The Sticky Ruler
potential_solutions.description: Put double-sided tape on the end of the flat plastic ruler. Since the plastic ruler is very thin, it easily slides into the narrow gap to press against the permission slip and pull it right up.

potential_solutions.title: The Fishing Line
potential_solutions.description: Tape the heavy coin to one end of the yarn so it will drop straight down the gap. Add chewed gum to the bottom of the coin, lower it like a fishing line until it hits the slip, and carefully pull it up.

potential_solutions.title: The Wire Hook
potential_solutions.description: Untwist the wire coat hanger into one long, thin metal string. Bend a tiny little hook at the very end, slide it down the narrow space, and scoop it under the paper to drag it up to the top.

title: The Great Bus Pass Panic
complaint: Hi! I'm Ethan. I am standing in the school hallway right as the final bell rings, but I just dropped my school bus pass down a narrow floor grate and my bus leaves in exactly three minutes!
obvious_trap: Tie the fridge magnet to the yarn and lower it down the grate to fish out the bus pass.
hidden_constraint: The bus pass is made entirely of thick plastic, so the magnet will not stick to it at all.

clue_cards.title: Sticky Situations
clue_cards.insight: Magnets only pull on certain metals. What else do you have that can grab onto a piece of smooth plastic?

clue_cards.title: Weight and See
clue_cards.insight: Yarn is very floppy and hard to aim on its own. You might need to tie something heavy to the end so it drops straight down.

clue_cards.title: Extended Reach
clue_cards.insight: If dropping a string is too hard to aim, maybe you can tape smaller things together to build a longer reaching tool.

potential_solutions.title: The Sticky Pendulum
potential_solutions.description: Chew a piece of gum and press it onto the heavy paperclip. Tie the paperclip to the yarn, then lower it down the grate so the gum sticks to the plastic bus pass and lifts it out.

potential_solutions.title: The Inside-Out Tape Drop
potential_solutions.description: Wrap scotch tape around the fridge magnet with the sticky side facing out. Tie the yarn around the taped magnet, using the magnet only as a heavy weight to drop the sticky tape directly onto the pass.

potential_solutions.title: The Straw Extension Pole
potential_solutions.description: Tape the plastic drinking straw to the end of the wooden ruler to make it longer and thin enough to fit through the grate. Stick a piece of chewed gum on the end of the straw to reach down and grab the pass.

title: The Whistle in the Pipe
complaint: Hi! I'm Aria. I have to leave for my soccer championship in exactly five minutes, but I accidentally dropped the captain's whistle down a deep, narrow metal pipe sticking out of the ground!
obvious_trap: Tie a fridge magnet to a shoelace and lower it down the pipe to catch the whistle.
hidden_constraint: The whistle is made of brightly colored hard plastic, not metal, so a magnet will not stick to it at all.
on_hand_items: a large plastic water bottle full of water

clue_cards.title: Magnetic Match
clue_cards.insight: Magnets are super helpful for picking things up, but they only work on certain metals. Before trying to fish it out, you should find out what the whistle is actually made of!

clue_cards.title: Sticky Situation
clue_cards.insight: If a magnet won't stick, maybe you can make your own sticky grabber. You need something heavy enough to drop down the pipe, and something sticky to grab the whistle.

clue_cards.title: Rising Tide
clue_cards.insight: If the pipe is sealed in the ground, think about how hollow plastic acts in the bathtub. You might be able to make the whistle come to you without reaching down at all!

potential_solutions.title: The Sticky Weight
potential_solutions.description: Chew a piece of bubblegum to make it sticky, then press it onto the heavy pebble. Tie the shoelace around the pebble and lower it down the pipe to press the gum onto the plastic whistle and pull it up.

potential_solutions.title: The Fishing Hook
potential_solutions.description: Unbend the metal paperclip into a J-hook shape. Tie the shoelace to the paperclip, lower it down the pipe, and hook it through the little hole on the back of the whistle where a necklace usually goes.

potential_solutions.title: The Floater
potential_solutions.description: Pour all the water from the large water bottle straight down into the narrow metal pipe. Because the whistle is made of hollow plastic, it will float on the water right up to the top of the pipe so Aria can grab it.

title: The Vent of No Return
complaint: Hi! I'm Noah. I have exactly five minutes before my airport shuttle arrives for my honeymoon, but I just dropped my only car key down the narrow floor heating vent and the metal grate is painted shut to the hardwood!
obvious_trap: Tying the strong fridge magnet to the sewing thread to lower it down and magnetically pull the key out.
hidden_constraint: The key is a modern electronic fob with a heavy plastic casing and a solid brass backup blade; brass and plastic are non-magnetic, so the magnet won't grab it.
on_hand_items: A roll of double-sided carpet tape

clue_cards.title: Think Sticky, Not Magnetic
clue_cards.insight: If magnets won't attract the item, you will need to rely on a strong adhesive to grab hold of the heavy plastic casing.

clue_cards.title: Rigid Reach
clue_cards.insight: Thread and shoelaces are too floppy to aim accurately in a dark, narrow space. You need something stiff to guide your tool.

clue_cards.title: Physical Snag
clue_cards.insight: If adhesives fail, look for an item that is thin enough to slip through the grate but strong enough to be bent into a custom hook.

potential_solutions.title: The Sticky Stick
potential_solutions.description: Wrap a generous amount of double-sided carpet tape around the end of the long wooden paint stirrer. Shine the flashlight down to aim, push the stick through the grate, and press the tape firmly against the plastic key fob to pull it straight up.

potential_solutions.title: The Gum and Wire Harpoon
potential_solutions.description: Untwist the wire coat hanger so it forms a long, straight rod. Chew a piece of gum until it is extremely sticky, mold it over the tip of the wire, and use the rigid wire to press the gum hard onto the key to lift it out.

potential_solutions.title: The Precision Hook
potential_solutions.description: Use the metal spoon to help bend the very tip of the wire coat hanger into a tight, narrow hook. Use the flashlight to spot the metal key ring attached to the fob, carefully slide the wire hook through the ring, and fish it out.

title: The Five-Minute Flash Drive
complaint: Hi! I'm Lily. I'm in the office print room preparing for the biggest client pitch of my career starting in exactly five minutes, but the only flash drive holding my slide deck just slipped out of my hand and fell down a deep, narrow gap behind the massive, bolted-down industrial printer!
obvious_trap: Tying the fridge magnet to the yarn to lower it down the gap and magnetically fish out the dropped flash drive.
hidden_constraint: The flash drive casing is made entirely of lightweight aluminum and plastic, so it is completely non-magnetic and the magnet will not stick to it.
on_hand_items: a stack of heavy cardstock paper

clue_cards.title: Material Matters
clue_cards.insight: Magnets are great for picking up steel, but you might want to think about what the outside of a modern flash drive is actually made of.

clue_cards.title: Rigid Reach
clue_cards.insight: Yarn is floppy and hard to control in a tight space. You need something stiff that you can steer exactly where you want it.

clue_cards.title: Alternative Attraction
clue_cards.insight: If magnetism won't grab the drive, look for items that can create a strong, temporary physical bond.

potential_solutions.title: The Sticky Rod
potential_solutions.description: Unbend the wire coat hanger to create a long, rigid reacher. Wrap a piece of double-sided tape firmly around the tip, lower it down the gap, and press it directly onto the plastic flash drive to lift it out.

potential_solutions.title: The Gum Harpoon
potential_solutions.description: Chew a piece of gum until it is soft and extremely sticky. Mold it securely onto the very end of the wooden ruler, carefully guide it down the narrow gap, and press it firmly against the drive to pull it up.

potential_solutions.title: The Cardstock Scoop
potential_solutions.description: Fold a piece of heavy cardstock paper in half lengthwise to create a long, stiff V-shaped trough. Slide this trough down the wall to scoop perfectly under the flash drive, then use the unbent coat hanger to trap the drive against the paper while you pull both up together.

setting: Street Parking Next to a Storm Drain
title: The Drain Delay
complaint: Hi! I'm Jackson. I'm already ten minutes late for the final round of a massive job interview, but as I was unlocking my car, I fumbled and dropped my keys through a narrow grate into a deep storm drain!
obvious_trap: Tying a strong fridge magnet to a string to easily fish the metallic keys out of the drain.
hidden_constraint: Modern car keys and electronic fobs are made of solid brass and plastic, which are completely non-magnetic. Additionally, the storm drain slots are exactly one inch wide, blocking hands or thick items.

clue_cards.title: Material Check
clue_cards.insight: Don't assume all metal is the same. Modern car keys are cut from brass to prevent rusting, meaning standard magnets won't stick to them at all.

clue_cards.title: Sizing up the Gap
clue_cards.insight: The grate slots are incredibly narrow. Thick items like the broomstick won't fit. You need something thin, flexible, or droppable.

clue_cards.title: Alternate Attachments
clue_cards.insight: If magnetism fails, you only have two ways to grab an item at the bottom of a dark hole: hooking the key ring or using something incredibly sticky.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 1: The Sticky Plumb Bob
potential_solutions.description: Chew a piece of gum until it is highly sticky, press it firmly onto the heavy metal hex nut, and tie the hex nut to the long shoelace. Drop it directly onto the plastic surface of the key fob, press down lightly, and pull it up through the grate.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 2: The Tape Measure Claw
potential_solutions.description: Pull out a few feet of the metal tape measure and lock it so it stays rigid. Fold a piece of duct tape so the sticky side is facing outward, stick it to the end of the tape measure, and slide this rigid tool down the narrow grate to stick to the keys and pull them out.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 3: The Wire Hook
potential_solutions.description: Untwist the wire coat hanger completely to form a long, stiff wire. Bend a tiny hook into the very end. Shine the pocket flashlight down the drain to see the keys, slide the wire through the one-inch slot, hook the actual metal key ring, and carefully lift it to freedom.

title: The Gridlock Grate
complaint: Hi! I'm Emma. I'm in my hotel lobby waiting for my ride to a huge investor pitch, and I just dropped my critical presentation thumb drive down a narrow decorative floor grate!
obvious_trap: Tying the souvenir fridge magnet to the shoelace to lower it down and magnetically pull the thumb drive up.
hidden_constraint: The thumb drive casing is made of non-magnetic aluminum, and the grate slots are too narrow for the fridge magnet to fit through anyway.

clue_cards.title: Sticky Situation
clue_cards.insight: If magnets don't work on the material, think about what adhesives you have that can grab smooth metal.

clue_cards.title: Extending Your Reach
clue_cards.insight: The grate slots are very narrow. You need something thin and rigid to poke through the holes to reach the drive.

clue_cards.title: Cowgirl Up
clue_cards.insight: Shoelaces can do more than tie shoes. A simple loop might be able to hook around the drive if guided properly.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 1: The Sticky Stick
potential_solutions.description: Chew a piece of gum to make it sticky, press it firmly onto the end of the wooden coffee stirrer, and carefully lower it through the narrow grate to grab the thumb drive.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 2: The Nail File Grab
potential_solutions.description: Wrap double-sided tape around the tip of the metal nail file, lower it straight down through the grate, and press the sticky side flat against the aluminum body of the thumb drive to pull it up.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 3: The Shoelace Lasso
potential_solutions.description: Tie a small slipknot at the end of a sneaker shoelace. Use the metal nail file or coffee stirrer to guide the loop over the thumb drive, pull the lace tight, and hoist it out.

title: The Grate Escape
complaint: Hi! I'm Lucas. I am in the lobby of a corporate high-rise with exactly five minutes until the most important investor pitch of my career, but my USB drive holding the only copy of my presentation just slipped out of my hand and dropped straight through a narrow metal floor grate into a shallow gap below!
obvious_trap: Tying the souvenir fridge magnet to the long shoelace and lowering it down the grate to magnetically snap onto the USB drive and pull it up.
hidden_constraint: The USB drive features a premium brushed aluminum and plastic casing, meaning it is completely non-magnetic. The magnet will not pick it up, wasting precious time.

clue_cards.title: Clue 1: Ditch the Magnet
clue_cards.insight: If magnetism won't work on premium metals, you need to rely on adhesion. What items do you have that can stick to anything?

clue_cards.title: Clue 2: Need for Rigidity
clue_cards.insight: A dangling shoelace won't let you apply downward pressure. You need a tool that is long, skinny, and rigid to press down onto the lost item.

clue_cards.title: Clue 3: The Tongs Approach
clue_cards.insight: If sticking it doesn't work, maybe you can pinch it. Two long, straight objects can work together to lift something light.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 1: The Sticky Hanger
potential_solutions.description: Unwind the metal wire coat hanger until it forms a single long, stiff wire. Chew a piece of gum to make it highly sticky, press it firmly onto the end of the wire, lower it through the grate, and press down onto the USB drive to lift it out.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 2: Tape Measure Fishing
potential_solutions.description: Lock the retractable tape measure so it extends straight down into the grate. Stick a generous piece of double-sided tape to the flat metal tip of the tape measure, press it firmly onto the USB drive, and slowly reel it back up.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 3: Giant Chopstick Tweezers
potential_solutions.description: Slide the two long wooden chopsticks down through the grate slots. Keeping a steady hand, use the chopsticks like giant tongs to carefully pinch the sides of the USB drive and pull it vertically through the gap.

title: The Cafeteria Conundrum
complaint: Hi! I'm Mia. I am at the crowded school cafeteria looking for a seat, and my best friend Leo is sitting at a table deep in a very quiet conversation with a new kid I've never met.
obvious_trap: Walking right up, loudly saying 'Hey Leo!', and squeezing into the tight space between them to ask what they are talking about.
hidden_constraint: The new kid is extremely shy and easily startled by sudden interruptions, which would make them clam up and make Leo feel awkward.

clue_cards.title: Soft Approaches
clue_cards.insight: Sometimes, sliding into a conversation without using loud words is the best way not to startle a shy person.

clue_cards.title: Sharing is Caring
clue_cards.insight: Offering something small and nice can make a stranger feel welcome instead of feeling like their space is being invaded.

clue_cards.title: A Friendly Signal
clue_cards.insight: Passing a visual note or object gives them a chance to finish their thought and invite you in on their own time.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 1: The Origami Icebreaker
potential_solutions.description: Mia quietly approaches and slides the small origami paper crane across the table toward the new kid with a warm smile, waiting for them to notice and say hello first without interrupting the quiet chat.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 2: The Sticky Note Invite
potential_solutions.description: Mia uses the colorful markers to write a quick 'Hi, I'm Mia! Can I join you?' on the bright yellow sticky note, gently placing it on Leo's lunch tray so they can read it and invite her to sit.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 3: The Juice Box Offering
potential_solutions.description: Mia quietly walks up, gently sets the extra juice box down next to the new kid as a silent welcome gift, and takes an empty seat nearby, letting Leo introduce her naturally.

title: The Silent Signal
complaint: Hi! I'm Benjamin. I'm stuck at a very fancy dinner party and I really need to ask my dad for his phone to play games, but he is busy talking to his super strict boss at the other end of the long table!
obvious_trap: Folding a paper airplane note and throwing it across the table, or walking right up to tap Dad on the shoulder.
hidden_constraint: The strict boss gets very angry at any loud noises, kids interrupting, or things flying above the table. If the boss gets annoyed, Dad will definitely say no to the phone.

clue_cards.title: Out of Sight
clue_cards.insight: If the boss gets mad at things happening above the table, where is a place he definitely isn't looking?

clue_cards.title: Special Delivery
clue_cards.insight: You need a way to move your message across the floor without making a loud noise or showing your face to the boss.

clue_cards.title: Getting Attention
clue_cards.insight: Adults don't always look down while they are talking. How can you make your dad notice something at his feet without making a sound?

potential_solutions.title: The Under-Cover Car
potential_solutions.description: Write a polite note on the napkin with the red crayon. Use the hair tie to strap the napkin to the toy car, and gently roll it under the table to softly bump Dad's shoe without the boss seeing.

potential_solutions.title: The Sneaky String Pull
potential_solutions.description: Write a note on the napkin and attach it to the yarn using the paperclip. Crawl under the table where you are hidden, toss the paperclip end near Dad's foot, and gently tug the yarn to brush his leg so he looks down.

potential_solutions.title: The Flashlight Telegraph
potential_solutions.description: Write a note on the napkin, fold it, and slide it under the table near Dad's chair. Use the small pocket flashlight to shine a subtle beam on his shiny dress shoes to quietly make him look down and find the note.

title: The Cafeteria Clip Crisis
complaint: Hi! I'm Amelia. I'm at the school cafeteria sitting near the older kids' table, and my best friend accidentally kicked her favorite shiny hair clip right under their chairs! I need to get it back for her without crawling awkwardly under their feet or interrupting their intense group story.
obvious_trap: Crawling right under the table to grab it, or walking up and loudly asking them to move so you can poke around with a ruler.
hidden_constraint: The older kids have their giant backpacks blocking the front of the table like a wall, so you can only reach from a side angle where you can't see the clip. Plus, the girl telling the story gets highly offended if someone talks over her.
on_hand_items: A pack of sticky poster putty

clue_cards.title: Sight Without Staring
clue_cards.insight: Crawling on the floor near someone's feet is awkward. How can you look around a corner or behind a backpack without putting your head down there?

clue_cards.title: Silent Messages
clue_cards.insight: If talking out loud will interrupt a good story and cause offense, a written message can be read whenever the person is ready.

clue_cards.title: Sticky Situations
clue_cards.insight: If you can't reach something with your hands, maybe you can combine a few basic items to make a long tool that grabs things on contact.

potential_solutions.title: The Mirror and Sticky Stick
potential_solutions.description: Put sticky poster putty on the end of the wooden ruler. Place the pocket mirror on the floor at the side of the table so you can see behind the backpack wall, then gently guide the sticky ruler to grab the clip without ever making a sound or invading their personal space.

potential_solutions.title: The Polite Paper Airplane
potential_solutions.description: Write a polite, funny note on the notebook paper with the pink marker asking for help rescuing the shiny clip. Fold it into a paper airplane and gently glide it onto the center of their table. This asks for help in a fun way without verbally interrupting the storyteller.

potential_solutions.title: The Shoelace Bowling Ball
potential_solutions.description: Tape the bouncy ball to the end of the shoelace. Using the pocket mirror to aim from the side gap, gently swing the ball like a pendulum to knock the hair clip back over to your side of the cafeteria, remaining completely unnoticed.

title: The Sticky Situation
complaint: Hi! I'm James. I am sitting in the audience at the school talent show while the principal gives a very quiet, serious speech, but my best friend Sam is sitting three rows ahead with a highly embarrassing sticker stuck to his back!
obvious_trap: Crumpling up a sticky note into a ball or throwing the bouncy ball directly at Sam's head to quickly get his attention.
hidden_constraint: The principal is actively scanning the air above the crowd and will immediately halt the assembly if they see a flying object, and Sam gets extremely embarrassed and will cry if the whole room turns to look at a commotion.
on_hand_items: A pad of blank sticky notes

clue_cards.title: Floor Level Focus
clue_cards.insight: The principal is looking over the heads of the crowd to watch for troublemakers, but nobody is paying attention to the floor space under the seats.

clue_cards.title: Silent Signals
clue_cards.insight: Light travels completely silently, never counts as a thrown object, and won't make a loud thud if it hits someone.

clue_cards.title: The Buddy System
clue_cards.insight: Sometimes the best way to be polite and avoid a public scene is to ask the people sitting between you for a quiet, secret favor.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 1: The Under-Seat Delivery
potential_solutions.description: Write a quick warning on a sticky note and stick it to the flat plastic ruler. Tie the yarn through the hole in the ruler and slide it gently along the floor under the seats until it taps Sam's foot, keeping everything out of the principal's sight.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 2: The Silent Spotlight
potential_solutions.description: Turn on the keychain flashlight and use the pocket mirror to bounce a tiny beam of light onto Sam's lap. When he gets confused and turns around to see where the light is coming from, quietly hold up a sticky note with the warning written on it.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 3: The Secret Pass-Forward
potential_solutions.description: Write a polite note telling Sam to check his back, fold it up securely, and use a metal paperclip to keep it closed. Tap the shoulder of the kid in front of you and whisper a request to pass the note forward row by row until it reaches Sam without causing a scene.

title: The Silent Treatment Standoff
complaint: Hi! I'm Harper. My two best friends are sitting on the playground bench having a huge argument, and now they are giving each other the silent treatment.
obvious_trap: Walking right up to them, standing in the middle, and telling them they need to stop acting silly and apologize to each other.
hidden_constraint: Both friends are super embarrassed and proud. If Harper directly tells them what to do, they will feel ganged up on, get mad at her for being bossy, and walk away to different parts of the playground.

clue_cards.title: The Icebreaker
clue_cards.insight: Sometimes a shared laugh is much better than a forced apology when you want to get people talking again.

clue_cards.title: The Accidental Distraction
clue_cards.insight: Giving them a physical reason to interact that has nothing to do with their fight can instantly break the silent treatment.

clue_cards.title: The Silent Approach
clue_cards.insight: Words can make proud people feel defensive. Try communicating a fun idea without making a single sound.

potential_solutions.title: The Funny Note
potential_solutions.description: Use the blank notebook and crayons to draw a really silly picture of a three-headed monster. Slide the open notebook between them on the bench without saying a word. When they look at it, the shared laugh will melt the tension without anyone having to admit they were wrong.

potential_solutions.title: The Runaway Ball
potential_solutions.description: Pretend to trip and 'accidentally' drop the red bouncy ball so it rolls right under the bench between their feet. When they both naturally bend down to grab it for you at the same time, the awkward silence will be broken by the teamwork.

potential_solutions.title: The Light Chaser
potential_solutions.description: Stand far away and use the shiny pocket mirror to bounce a little spot of sunlight onto the ground near their shoes. Move it around quickly like a glowing bug until they both notice it, forget they are mad, and start trying to step on it together.

setting: An upscale business lunch with a major prospective client
title: The Spinach Standoff
complaint: Hi! I'm Alexander. I am sitting at an upscale business lunch with a major prospective client, but they have a massive piece of spinach stuck right in their front teeth and are about to give a toast to the whole room!
obvious_trap: Leaning over to quietly whisper in the client's ear about the spinach to save them from public embarrassment.
hidden_constraint: The client is severely hard of hearing and very touchy about personal space. If you try to whisper, they will loudly yell, 'WHAT? SPEAK UP!' drawing the entire room's attention to the awkward situation.

clue_cards.title: Mirror Neurons
clue_cards.insight: People naturally mimic the actions of others in social settings. Drawing attention to your own face might subconsciously make them check theirs.

clue_cards.title: The Written Word
clue_cards.insight: If verbal communication is too risky or loud, a private, silent message can save face without drawing outside attention.

clue_cards.title: The Digital Reflection
clue_cards.insight: Sometimes people just need to see themselves to realize something is wrong. A modern device can act as an impromptu mirror.

potential_solutions.title: The Silent Note
potential_solutions.description: Write a polite, discreet note on the back of the blank business card with the ballpoint pen ('Quick heads up: a little food in your teeth!') and slide it under their leather-bound menu where only they will see it.

potential_solutions.title: The Sympathy Check
potential_solutions.description: Take out the compact mirror and the wooden toothpick. Subtly but visibly check your own teeth in the mirror. Social mirroring will prompt the client to feel self-conscious and check their own reflection in their cutlery or phone.

potential_solutions.title: The Selfie Distraction
potential_solutions.description: Take out your smartphone, open the front-facing camera, and politely ask the client to lean in for a quick photo to commemorate the successful lunch. They will see their own face on the screen and notice the spinach immediately before standing up.

title: The Spinach Standoff
complaint: Hi! I'm Evelyn. I'm sitting at a formal gala table next to my company's CEO, and he has a massive blob of spinach stuck right in his front teeth just minutes before his keynote speech.
obvious_trap: Leaning in to whisper in his ear about the spinach, or simply handing him a toothpick.
hidden_constraint: The CEO turned down his hearing aids because the live band is too loud, so whispering will make him yell 'WHAT?!' loudly. Additionally, handing him a toothpick directly will deeply offend his pride in front of the city mayor who is sitting directly across from him.
on_hand_items: A small packet of breath mints

clue_cards.title: Bypass the Ears
clue_cards.insight: If audio communication (whispering) is compromised by loud music and hearing aids, you must rely entirely on visual, silent communication.

clue_cards.title: The Mirroring Effect
clue_cards.insight: Humans are highly susceptible to psychological mirroring. If you draw attention to your own face or teeth, others will subconsciously check their own.

clue_cards.title: The Gift of Dignity
clue_cards.insight: Powerful people hate being corrected in front of peers. Giving them a tool to discover the error themselves preserves their ego.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 1: The Silent Note
potential_solutions.description: Write a quick, polite note on the blank business card using the ballpoint pen (e.g., 'Quick teeth check before your speech!'). Slide it discreetly onto his plate or under his glass where only he can see it, bypassing the hearing aid issue completely.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 2: The Pre-Speech Routine
potential_solutions.description: Take out the compact mirror, pretend to quickly check your own teeth or lipstick, and then casually offer the open mirror to the CEO, gesturing to the stage. He will accept the 'pre-speech check' as a common courtesy and see the spinach himself.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 3: The Empathy Mimic
potential_solutions.description: Catch the CEO's eye and conspicuously use the cloth dinner napkin to wipe your own front teeth. The psychological mirroring effect will prompt him to instinctively run his tongue over his own teeth, allowing him to feel the spinach without a word being spoken.

title: The Gala Tag Blunder
complaint: Hi! I'm Daniel. I'm sitting at the front table of our company's annual fundraising gala. My CEO just stepped up to the main podium, but he unknowingly has a bright neon draft note stuck upside-down over his official title badge on his suit jacket.
obvious_trap: Walking straight up to the stage podium to pull the embarrassing note off his suit jacket right before he speaks.
hidden_constraint: Live broadcast cameras and strict stage security are active; walking up directly will cause the camera to zoom in on the stage and broadcast the awkward commotion to thousands of online donors.
on_hand_items: A roll of clear double-sided tape
A stiff paper pocket note card
A folded white linen cloth napkin
A smartphone with a bright flashlight
A spare blank adhesive name badge

clue_cards.title: Indirect Redirection
clue_cards.insight: If you cannot walk onto the stage, prompt a silent natural reaction by using line-of-sight visual cues.

clue_cards.title: The Mirroring Effect
clue_cards.insight: People instinctively mirror actions they see in their direct gaze; pointing to or adjusting your own chest lapel usually triggers the observer to check theirs.

clue_cards.title: Backstage Communication
clue_cards.insight: The AV and stage crew have a direct line to the speaker via the monitor screen and teleprompter operators.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 1: The Mirroring Sight-Line Cue
potential_solutions.description: Write 'LAPEL NOTE' in bold letters on the stiff note card using the marker, stand directly behind the main camera line facing the CEO, hold up the card, and tap your own lapel so he mirrors the action and quietly removes the note himself.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 2: The Stagehand Relay
potential_solutions.description: Hand the spare blank name badge with a quick handwritten warning note to the backstage AV technician, allowing them to pass it discreetly to the CEO when delivering his podium water glass.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 3: The Light Reflection Signal
potential_solutions.description: Angle the stainless steel spoon to reflect a soft light beam onto the monitor desk in the stage wings, drawing the stage manager's attention so they can give the CEO a silent hand signal from off-camera.

title: The Diplomatic Rescue
complaint: Hi! I'm Abigail. I'm managing our keynote speaker at our annual gala, but he is currently trapped in a conversation with our most sensitive major donor just three minutes before he needs to go on stage.
obvious_trap: Walking directly up to them, cutting off the donor mid-sentence, and announcing that the speaker must leave for the stage immediately.
hidden_constraint: The major donor is hyper-sensitive to perceived slights; feeling cut off or dismissed will cause them to pull their $500,000 annual contribution on the spot.
on_hand_items: A smartphone with adjustable alarm sounds
A VIP staff badge on a lanyard

clue_cards.title: Praise Before Pulling
clue_cards.insight: People don't feel offended by an interruption if the distraction frames them as an essential VIP.

clue_cards.title: The Silent Visual Cue
clue_cards.insight: Passing a physical, official-looking document allows the speaker to excuse themselves without anyone losing face.

clue_cards.title: Shift the Focus
clue_cards.insight: Giving the donor a high-value task or introduction makes stepping away feel like an upgrade, not a dismissal.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 1: The Honored Escort Pivot
potential_solutions.description: Approach both of them, compliment the donor publicly on their impact, and invite the donor to walk the speaker down the front aisle so the donor receives front-row recognition as the speech begins.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 2: The Silent Stage Cue
potential_solutions.description: Hand a sealed white envelope marked 'Final Stage Opening Notes' directly to the speaker with a warm smile, giving the speaker an immediate, polite excuse to step away and review his notes.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 3: The High-Profile Hand-Off
potential_solutions.description: Bring over a tray of specialty drinks and excuse yourself to ask the donor if they would accept an exclusive interview with the event press team nearby, smoothly freeing up the speaker.

setting: A formal business dinner at a high-end restaurant
title: Spinach Sabotage
complaint: Hi! I'm Henry. I'm hosting a high-stakes contract dinner with an important client and my hot-tempered boss, but my boss has a large piece of spinach stuck right on his front tooth while making the pitch.
obvious_trap: Directly telling the boss about the spinach or handing him a toothpick across the table.
hidden_constraint: The boss is extremely self-conscious; any public callout or overt sign of dental grooming at the table causes him to feel humiliated and blow up, ruining the business deal.
on_hand_items: A glass of water with a lemon wedge
A smartphone with a front camera

clue_cards.title: The Mirroring Effect
clue_cards.insight: People naturally mirror body language; deliberately touching your own tooth while making eye contact often triggers a self-check.

clue_cards.title: Private Discretion
clue_cards.insight: Social blunders are best addressed out of earshot or via private visual notes that look like standard table interactions.

clue_cards.title: The Strategic Escort
clue_cards.insight: Creating a plausible excuse to stand up together allows for a quiet word away from the main table.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 1: Non-Verbal Mirror Cue
potential_solutions.description: Establish direct eye contact with the boss while wiping your own front tooth with a cloth napkin and giving a subtle, knowing nod, prompting him to reflexively mirror the motion and remove it unobserved.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 2: Menu Note Pass
potential_solutions.description: Write a discreet note on the paper cocktail napkin, tuck it inside the printed cardstock dinner menu, and pass it to the boss while verbally asking for his input on the dessert options.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 3: Restroom Side-Trip
potential_solutions.description: Excuse yourself to the restroom and quietly ask the boss to step aside with you for a quick 'strategy check' before the bill arrives, informing him privately once away from the client.

title: The Missing Detective Badge
complaint: Hi! I'm Ella. I'm playing detective in the school library playroom, but my special shiny detective badge dropped through the narrow floor grate under the radiator!
obvious_trap: Lowering a strong horseshoe magnet on a shoelace down the grate to stick to the shiny silver badge.
hidden_constraint: The shiny silver badge is made of lightweight toy plastic coated in metallic foil, so it is completely non-magnetic.

clue_cards.title: Shiny Isn't Always Magnetic
clue_cards.insight: Toy badges often look like metal steel, but a magnet won't grab plastic covered in silver paint.

clue_cards.title: Check the Back of the Badge
clue_cards.insight: Every detective badge has a small safety pin loop on the back that a small hook can catch onto.

clue_cards.title: Sticky Sticks to Everything
clue_cards.insight: Pressing something soft and tacky against a flat plastic surface creates a strong quick grab without needing magnets.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 1: Sticky Tool Extension
potential_solutions.description: Press the wad of sticky craft putty or reverse-wrapped duct tape onto the end of the long wooden yardstick, shine the flashlight to aim, and press it firmly down onto the flat plastic badge to lift it up.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 2: Wire Hook Fisherman
potential_solutions.description: Unbend the wire clothes hanger or metal paperclip into a small hook shape, tape it tightly to the end of the wooden yardstick, and snag the pin loop on the back of the badge.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 3: Long Tongs Extender
potential_solutions.description: Tape the handle of the long kitchen tongs securely to the end of the yardstick, use the shoelace tied to the lever to squeeze the tongs shut, and pinch the badge to pull it out.

title: The Trapped Clue Book
complaint: Hi! I'm Sebastian. I'm in my treehouse club room working on a top secret case, but my clue notebook just slipped into the tiny crack behind our huge wooden bookcase!
obvious_trap: Lower a strong magnet on a shoelace behind the bookcase to snap onto the shiny spiral spine of the notebook.
hidden_constraint: The shiny spiral spine on the notebook is made of soft plastic coil, not metal, so magnets cannot stick to it.
on_hand_items: a roll of sticky duct tape
a thin piece of cardboard from a cereal box

clue_cards.title: Test the Magnet First
clue_cards.insight: Try sticking your magnet to a extra notebook nearby to see if the spiral binding is actually metal.

clue_cards.title: Sticky Powers
clue_cards.insight: Sticky tape or gooey toys can grip smooth paper covers without needing any magnetism.

clue_cards.title: Hook the Loops
