obvious_trap: Lowering a strong magnet tied to a piece of string down into the air vent.
hidden_constraint: The wedding ring is solid gold and non-magnetic, and the air duct makes a sharp 90-degree turn just ten inches down.
on_hand_items: A small pack of blue sticky tack
A pair of rubber kitchen gloves

clue_cards.title: Metal Test
clue_cards.insight: Precious metals like gold, silver, and brass have zero magnetic pull, making magnetic tools useless.

clue_cards.title: Bending Corners
clue_cards.insight: Rigid broomsticks can't bypass sharp elbow joints in ductwork; you need something bendable that holds its shape.

clue_cards.title: Adhesive Reach
clue_cards.insight: Sticky tack or rolled tape on the tip of a malleable rod can pick up smooth items with direct pressure.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 1: Sticky Wire Probe
potential_solutions.description: Untwist the wire coat hanger, bend a curved angle at the end to match the duct's elbow, mold a firmly attached ball of sticky tack onto the tip, and press down onto the gold ring to pick it up.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 2: Inverted Tape Loop
potential_solutions.description: Shape the wire coat hanger to curve around the elbow bend, then wrap the tip with duct tape sticky-side-out to create a pliable adhesive snare that grabs the ring.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 3: Glove Finger Press
potential_solutions.description: Cut the finger tip off a rubber kitchen glove, stretch it over a bent wire end, and coat it with sticky tack to create a soft, high-friction press tool that pulls the ring back around the corner.

setting: Utility room in Gracie's basement apartment
title: Key Down the Drain
complaint: Hi! I'm Gracie. I was unlocking the basement storage room when my main brass key ring slipped out of my hand and fell right down a narrow floor drain pipe behind the water heater!
obvious_trap: Lowering a fridge magnet tied to dental floss, or sticking duct tape to the tip of a straight wire coat hanger to pull the keys up.
hidden_constraint: The keys are solid brass and completely non-magnetic, the pipe has an elbow bend at the bottom, and standing water inside instantly ruins duct tape stickiness.
on_hand_items: A pair of rubber dishwashing gloves

clue_cards.title: Material Check
clue_cards.insight: Magnets only stick to iron and steel. Solid brass keys won't react to magnetic pull no matter how strong the magnet is.

clue_cards.title: Waterproof Tack
clue_cards.insight: Standard tape adhesive loses all grip when submerged in water, but chewed gum retains sticky elasticity underwater.

clue_cards.title: Bending Around Corners
clue_cards.insight: A rigid straight stick jams at pipe elbows; flexible guides or a cinch loop can travel past turns easily.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 1: The Straw Snare
potential_solutions.description: Double a long strand of dental floss and thread it through a flexible drinking straw so a loop sticks out the bottom end. Lower the straw past the pipe elbow, maneuver the loop around the brass keyring, pull the top floss strands tight to lock the snare, and lift the keys out.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 2: Gum-Tipped Wire Grabber
potential_solutions.description: Chew a piece of stick gum until soft and mold it firmly onto a small hook bent at the end of the wire coat hanger. Push the wire down past the bend into the water puddle; press the gum onto the keys to stick onto them underwater and retrieve them.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 3: Umbrella Rib Hook
potential_solutions.description: Remove one thin, springy metal rib from the foldable umbrella. Bend the end into a tiny sharp J-hook. Because the umbrella rib is flexible enough to curve through the elbow bend without jamming, feed it down, hook the keyring loop, and draw it up.

title: The Vent Token Drop
complaint: Hi! I'm Grayson. I was playing in my bedroom showing off my special shiny star token, but it bounced across the rug and fell right through the narrow slats of the floor vent!
obvious_trap: Lowering a strong magnet tied to a shoelace down into the vent to snap onto the metal token.
hidden_constraint: The star token is made of solid painted aluminum, so magnets will not stick to it at all.
on_hand_items: A pair of sneakers with long shoelaces
A roll of sticky duct tape
A wad of sticky blue mounting tack
A pair of long kitchen tongs

clue_cards.title: Test the Attraction
clue_cards.insight: Not all shiny metals are pulled by magnets—aluminum and brass won't stick!

clue_cards.title: Sticky Touch
clue_cards.insight: Items with sticky surfaces work on almost any flat, smooth object regardless of material.

clue_cards.title: Hook & Lift
clue_cards.insight: A thin, bendable wire can be shaped into tiny hooks or scoops to catch edges or loops.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 1: Sticky Ruler Probe
potential_solutions.description: Press a thick wad of sticky blue mounting tack onto the end of the long wooden ruler, shine the flashlight down the vent, and press the stick firmly onto the token to lift it straight out.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 2: Wire Hook Retrieval
potential_solutions.description: Unbend the wire coat hanger and form a small hook at the tip, then fish it down the vent slot to catch the star token's top loop and pull it up.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 3: Tape Scoop Tool
potential_solutions.description: Cut the bottom off the empty plastic soda bottle to form a tiny scoop, attach it securely to the shoelace, and lower it down to scoop under the token and retrieve it.

title: The Vanished Star Medallion
complaint: Hi! I'm Jayden. I'm putting the final touches on my awesome cardboard robot at my garage invention station, but my special glow-in-the-dark star medallion slipped right down the narrow crack behind the giant, unmovable wooden workbench!
obvious_trap: Dangling a strong magnet down the gap on a string to quickly snap the medallion up.
hidden_constraint: The medallion is made of glow-in-the-dark plastic and solid brass, so magnets won't stick to it at all.
on_hand_items: a roll of double-sided sticky tape
a blob of blue poster tack

clue_cards.title: Test the Attraction
clue_cards.insight: Check what material the medallion is made of before trying magnetic tricks!

clue_cards.title: Sticky Touch
clue_cards.insight: Objects that aren't magnetic can still stick to strong tape or tacky putty if pressed firmly.

clue_cards.title: Hook and Ring
clue_cards.insight: The medallion has a small loop at the top for a necklace chain—perfect for a thin hook.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 1: Sticky Ruler Pick
potential_solutions.description: Wrap double-sided sticky tape around the tip of the wooden ruler, shine the flashlight down the gap, and press the taped end firmly onto the flat surface of the medallion to lift it up.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 2: Wire Hook Retriever
potential_solutions.description: Untwist the wire coat hanger into a long straight rod with a small hook at the end, then lower it down to latch directly into the medallion's top ring.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 3: Tack-on-a-Stick
potential_solutions.description: Press a thick ball of blue poster tack onto the end of the ruler, reach down into the tight space, and push down hard onto the plastic star so it sticks for retrieval.

title: The Lost Shiny Medal
complaint: Hi! I'm Stella. I was showing off my lucky science fair medal in the craft room, but it bounced right off the table and fell into a super narrow crack under the heavy wooden cabinet!
obvious_trap: Tie a magnet to a string and lower it down into the crack to pull the metal medal right out.
hidden_constraint: The lucky medal is made of solid brass, which is a non-magnetic metal, so the magnet will not stick to it.
on_hand_items: A pair of long wooden chopsticks
A blob of reusable poster putty

clue_cards.title: Test the Metal
clue_cards.insight: Not all shiny metals are magnetic! Test your magnet on the spare brass materials first to see if it even sticks.

clue_cards.title: Sticky Power
clue_cards.insight: Sticky stuff like tape or putty can cling to smooth metal surfaces even when magnets won't work.

clue_cards.title: Extend Your Reach
clue_cards.insight: Attach a sticky material to the end of a long stick to reach deep into narrow spaces.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 1: The Sticky Tape Stick
potential_solutions.description: Wrap duct tape sticky-side-out around the end of a long wooden chopstick, lower it down onto the brass medal, press down tightly, and lift it straight up out of the crack.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 2: Putty Press
potential_solutions.description: Stick a firm ball of poster putty onto the tip of the long metal spoon handle, push it down onto the flat top of the medal, and pull it back up carefully.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 3: The Straw Scoop
potential_solutions.description: Flatten the end of the flexible plastic straw to create a thin wedge, slide it underneath the medal, and lift it up out of the floor gap.

title: The Shiny Badge Rescue
complaint: Hi! I'm Gabriel. I'm building a cardboard robot in my treehouse lab, but my favorite shiny silver robot badge slipped through a tiny crack behind my workbench!
obvious_trap: Tying the horseshoe magnet to the spool of yarn and dropping it down the gap to magnetic-ally pick up the shiny badge.
hidden_constraint: The shiny badge is made of lightweight plastic covered in foil wrap, so magnets will not stick to it at all.
on_hand_items: A roll of double-sided sticky tape
A toy dart with a rubber suction cup

clue_cards.title: Material Inspection
clue_cards.insight: Not everything that shines like shiny silver is actually magnetic!

clue_cards.title: Sticky Surfaces
clue_cards.insight: Tape or sticky tack can easily grab smooth plastic items that magnets ignore.

clue_cards.title: Narrow Reach
clue_cards.insight: A long flat wooden ruler easily slides into deep, narrow gaps.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 1: Sticky Ruler Dip
potential_solutions.description: Wrap double-sided sticky tape around the end of the long wooden ruler, slide it down the narrow crack, press it onto the badge, and pull it back up.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 2: Sticky Tack Wand
potential_solutions.description: Attach a lump of sticky tack to the end of the long ruler, lower it down into the gap, and press firmly against the badge to stick to it and lift it out.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 3: Suction Cup Drop
potential_solutions.description: Tie yarn to the toy suction cup dart, drop it straight down the gap onto the smooth plastic surface of the badge, press gently, and lift the badge out.

title: The Vent Drop Rescue
complaint: Hi! I'm Isaac. I was showing off my favorite glow-in-the-dark secret agent ring in my room, but it bounced right off my desk and plunged deep into the floor air vent!
obvious_trap: Lowering a magnet on a string down the vent to stick to the ring and pull it back up.
hidden_constraint: The secret agent ring is made of glow-in-the-dark plastic, so magnets will not attract it at all.
on_hand_items: A roll of double-sided sticky tape
A tub of squishy play dough
A pair of plastic kitchen tongs

clue_cards.title: Material Check
clue_cards.insight: Not all shiny gadgets are made of metal! Check if the item is magnetic first.

clue_cards.title: Reach and Stick
clue_cards.insight: Items that aren't magnetic can still stick to tacky surfaces or squishy dough.

clue_cards.title: Hooking Strategy
clue_cards.insight: Rings have a large hole in the center that is perfect for catching with a hook.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 1: Sticky Ruler Pick
potential_solutions.description: Wrap double-sided sticky tape around the bottom tip of the wooden ruler, shine the flashlight down the vent to locate the plastic ring, and press the taped end onto the ring to stick to it and pull it straight up.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 2: Wire Hook Retriever
potential_solutions.description: Unbend the wire coat hanger into a long straight rod and bend a tiny hook shape at the bottom end. Lower it into the vent, loop the hook through the middle of the ring, and carefully lift it out.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 3: Dough Press Stamp
potential_solutions.description: Press a wad of sticky play dough onto the end of the wooden ruler, lower it down the vent onto the ring, and push down gently so the plastic ring embeds into the dough before pulling it up.

title: Trapped Prototype
complaint: Hi! I'm Willow. I was testing our brand-new smart key fob in the design studio, but it accidentally dropped right down inside a six-foot-tall clear acrylic sensor tube mounted vertically against the wall, and I need to retrieve it before tomorrow morning's investor pitch!
obvious_trap: Lowering a strong magnet attached to a string down the tube to snap onto the metallic-looking key fob and pull it straight back up.
hidden_constraint: The key fob's outer shell is made of high-end anodized aluminum and carbon fiber, rendering it completely non-magnetic.
on_hand_items: a roll of heavy-duty double-sided tape
a small tub of sticky adhesive putty
a shop vacuum with a narrow nozzle
a pair of rubber-dipped grip gloves
a bundle of plastic drinking straws

clue_cards.title: Material Check
clue_cards.insight: Not all shiny metals attract magnets; test or inspect the object's true surface material before relying on magnetic force.

clue_cards.title: Adhesive Grip
clue_cards.insight: Pressing a sticky material firmly against a flat, dry surface can create enough surface grip to lift lightweight objects.

clue_cards.title: Mechanical Loop
clue_cards.insight: If an item has a ring or loop attached, catching it physically with a slipknot loop bypasses sticky or magnetic requirements entirely.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 1: Sticky Probe Retrieve
potential_solutions.description: Affix a wad of sticky adhesive putty or double-sided tape to the tip of the flexible fiberglass rod, guide it down to press onto the key fob's flat top, and slowly lift the fob out.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 2: Vacuum Suction Lift
potential_solutions.description: Attach the narrow nozzle to the shop vacuum hose, feed the hose down into the tube, turn on the power to create air suction against the fob, and pull it smoothly to the top.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 3: String Loop Snare
potential_solutions.description: Tie a small slipknot in the cotton string and guide the loop using the fiberglass rod around the key fob's keyring, then pull the string taut to cinch the loop and pull the fob up.

title: The Glass Prototype Pitfall
complaint: Hi! I'm Character_57. I'm prepping for our big midnight investor demo in the lab, but my delicate glass prototype slide slipped and fell into a pitch-black, tight gap under our heavy steel worktable.
obvious_trap: Tying the neodymium magnet to the string and fishing around under the table to grab the prototype.
hidden_constraint: The glass slide is entirely non-magnetic, and the floor underneath is covered in thick machine oil that will permanently smudge the slide if dragged along the ground.
on_hand_items: Can of compressed air with nozzle tube

clue_cards.title: Angles and Illumination
clue_cards.insight: Use the mirror and light together to see beneath the table without blindly poking around in the oil.

clue_cards.title: Sticky Touch, No Dragging
clue_cards.insight: Wrapped tape on a thin tool lets you touch the top surface of non-magnetic items to lift them cleanly vertical.

clue_cards.title: Puff and Float
clue_cards.insight: A soft blast of compressed air can push lightweight items across slippery surfaces without touching them directly.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 1: Sticky-Ruler Top Lift
potential_solutions.description: Spot the slide using the mirror and flashlight, wrap masking tape sticky-side-out onto the tip of the flexible ruler, press down lightly on the dry top corner of the glass slide, and lift it straight up off the oiled floor.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 2: Silicone Spatula Scoop
potential_solutions.description: Slide the flat silicone spatula beneath the slide to act as a clean barrier, cradling the bottom of the glass off the messy floor before sliding both out together.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 3: Air-Blast Drift
potential_solutions.description: Aim the compressed air nozzle tube at the far corner of the glass slide and give short gentle bursts to glide the slide across the slick floor onto a clean sheet of paper placed at the gap opening.

title: The Locked Slot Setback
complaint: Hi! I'm Character_57. I'm trapped in our prototyping shop twenty minutes before our biggest investor demo, and my unique master prototype key just slipped out of my hand. It plummeted directly into a narrow floor drain slot positioned beneath a heavy, bolted-down steel workbench, completely out of arm's reach.
obvious_trap: Lowering a strong magnet tied to a piece of string down the drain to quickly snap onto the key and pull it up.
hidden_constraint: The prototype key is custom-machined from solid brass and anodized aluminum, making it entirely non-magnetic, and the drain slot opening is less than half an inch wide.
on_hand_items: A roll of double-sided mounting tape
A tube of quick-setting gel glue
A pair of long wooden chopsticks

clue_cards.title: Metal Check
clue_cards.insight: Not all shiny metal metals react to magnets; brass and aluminum won't budge no matter how strong the magnet is.

clue_cards.title: Sticky Contact
clue_cards.insight: Adhesives need solid direct pressure on a flat, dry surface to lift weight without sliding off.

clue_cards.title: Width Limits
clue_cards.insight: Anything wider than 0.4 inches will scrape against the drain edges and drop whatever it is carrying.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 1: Adhesive Dowel Probe
potential_solutions.description: Wrap a tiny, flat strip of double-sided mounting tape smoothly around the tip of the slim wooden dowel rod, lower it precisely down the center of the drain slot, press firm contact onto the top face of the key, and lift it vertically out.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 2: Wire Hook Loop Pick
potential_solutions.description: Unfold the thin wire coat hanger into a single straight wire with a tiny 0.2-inch L-bend at the bottom tip, lower it through the narrow slot, pass through the key's keyring hole, twist 90 degrees, and hook it up directly.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 3: Dual Chopstick Friction Pinch
potential_solutions.description: Lower both long wooden chopsticks down opposite sides of the narrow drain slot, wedge them against the sides of the key, use the top ends as a lever to pinch tight, and draw the key upward smoothly.

title: The Ring in the Pipe
complaint: Hi! I'm Character_57. I dropped a custom steel ring prototype down a narrow one-inch drain pipe under my workbench, and it's trapped three feet down just past a sharp elbow bend!
obvious_trap: Lowering a strong magnet tied to a string down the drain pipe to grab the steel ring.
hidden_constraint: The elbow joint of the pipe is held inside a heavy iron wall bracket, causing any lowered magnet to instantly slam against the inner pipe wall and freeze before reaching the ring.
on_hand_items: A spool of strong dental floss
A tube of fast-drying super glue
A bottle of liquid dish soap

clue_cards.title: Bypass Magnetic Force
clue_cards.insight: Since magnets get pulled into the iron pipe walls, look for lightweight physical items that can expand or stick on contact.

clue_cards.title: Inflatable Wedge
clue_cards.insight: An uninflated item can slip into tight gaps; inflating it creates pressure to grip or push objects from below.

clue_cards.title: Shielded Tip
clue_cards.insight: To lower sticky tape or glue down a pipe without touching the walls, protect the sides while keeping the leading tip active.

potential_solutions.title: Balloon Elevator Method
potential_solutions.description: Feed the flexible straw with the uninflated balloon taped securely to its tip down past the elbow and past the ring, blow through the straw to inflate the balloon underneath the ring, and gently lift the inflated balloon up to carry the ring out.

potential_solutions.title: Shielded Glue Probe
potential_solutions.description: Bend the wire coat hanger to navigate the elbow, wrap tape along the sides to keep it off the pipe walls, apply a drop of super glue to the top tip, press it onto the ring face for 20 seconds, and pull the bonded wire straight back up.

potential_solutions.title: Floss Slipknot Snare
potential_solutions.description: Form an adjustable slipknot loop with dental floss around the end of the flexible coat hanger wire, guide the loop over the upright band of the ring, pull the floss line tight to cinch around the ring, and carefully hoist it out.

setting: A late-night innovation lab and prototyping workshop
title: The Locked-Away Dongle
complaint: Hi! I'm Character_57. I'm putting the final touches on our prototype presentation in the innovation lab, but I accidentally dropped our security dongle down the narrow access slot under the fixed workbench, and the presentation starts in twenty minutes!
obvious_trap: Wrapping sticky duct tape inside-out around a wooden ruler to stick to the dongle and pull it straight up.
hidden_constraint: The slot entry is lined with dense dust-protection bristles that strip away stickiness from tape, and the slot curves at an angle that jams rigid rulers.
on_hand_items: A rubber suction cup from a desk organizer
An empty flexible plastic soda bottle

clue_cards.title: Rethink Rigidity
clue_cards.insight: Straight rigid tools like rulers jam in curved slots. Flexible tools can easily bend around corners to reach deep spaces.

clue_cards.title: Bypass the Bristles
clue_cards.insight: Adhesives get wiped clean by the entry bristles. Mechanical grip, suction, or hooking will work much better than tape.

clue_cards.title: Catching from Below
clue_cards.insight: Curved sheet plastic can be trimmed into a flexible slide that scoops under small objects to lift them without needing adhesive.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 1: The Suction Snake
potential_solutions.description: Tie the rubber suction cup securely to the end of the flexible plastic measuring tape using nylon string. Push the flexible measuring tape past the bristles and press the suction cup firmly onto the dongle's smooth surface to seal and lift it out cleanly.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 2: The Paperclip Lasso
potential_solutions.description: Unbend a metal paperclip into a flexible hook and attach it securely to a long shoelace. Bend the flexible plastic measuring tape alongside it to guide the hook past the bristles and through the dongle's key-ring loop to hoist it out.

potential_solutions.title: Solution 3: The Curved Plastic Scoop
potential_solutions.description: Use the steel scissors to cut the empty flexible plastic soda bottle into a smooth, curved plastic scoop strip. Slide the flexible strip past the bristles so it cradles under the dongle, then carefully pull both ends upward to cradle and retrieve it.
